overview: In Jainism, the concept of Tattvas refers to the fundamental principles or realities that form the basis of understanding the universe and guiding ethical conduct. The Tattvas are integral to daily conduct as they provide a framework for living a life in accordance with Jain principles. The primary Tattvas include Jiva (soul), Ajiva (non-soul), Asrava (influx of karmas), Bandha (bondage of karmas), Samvara (stoppage of karmas), Nirjara (shedding of karmas), and Moksha (liberation). Daily conduct in Jainism emphasizes the practice of non-violence (Ahimsa), truthfulness (Satya), non-stealing (Asteya), chastity (Brahmacharya), and non-possessiveness (Aparigraha), which are directly influenced by understanding and applying the Tattvas. By recognizing the impact of actions on the soul and the accumulation of karmas, Jains strive to minimize harm and adhere to strict ethical guidelines. This practice is seen in various aspects of daily life, such as dietary choices, interactions with others, and engagement in rituals, all aimed at reducing karmic bondage and progressing towards liberation.

primary_sources.title: Tattvartha Sutra
primary_sources.author: Umasvati
primary_sources.translation: The realities are soul, non-soul, influx, bondage, stoppage, shedding, and liberation.
primary_sources.notes: This sutra succinctly encapsulates the essence of Jain metaphysics and ethical practice.

misconceptions.myth: Tattvas are only metaphysical concepts with no practical application.
misconceptions.reality: Tattvas are foundational to Jain ethical practices and directly influence daily conduct, guiding adherents in making decisions that align with spiritual goals.
